rows.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
rows.claim: Some early readers hamzated أدرأتكم, apparently deriving it from دربت بكذا; Ibn Qutayba says this is mistaken.
rows.anchor: بعض المتقدمين: ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدرأتكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed reader treated الشياطون as a sound masculine plural; Ibn Qutayba presents it as a mistaken reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ: وما تنزلت به الشياطون

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: Another reader opened tāʾ, kasrated mīm, and made الأعداء accusative; Ibn Qutayba derives the phrase from أشمت الله العدو, not شمت الله العدو.
rows.anchor: وقرأ آخر: فلا تشمت بي الأعداء

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports reciting this before Ibrahim and Talha; they objected, while he replied that they had made the error.
rows.anchor: الأعمش قرأت عند إبراهيم وطلحة بن مصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya b. Waththab, followed by al-Aʿmash and Hamza, read this as ولاية; Ibn Qutayba prefers تلووا, bias in testimony, supported by 3:78.
rows.anchor: يحيى بن وثاب : وإن تلوا أو تعرضوا

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, followed by Hamza, kasrated the yāʾ as though the bāʾ governed the whole word; Ibn Qutayba rejects that case analysis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: وما أنتم بمصرخي

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza made the first السيئ jussive, though jussive mood does not govern nouns, while declinably reading the identical noun later.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة: ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi kasrated the nūn; Ibn Qutayba says the intended sense requires تبشرونني with two nūns because the pronoun occupies a nominative position.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع : فبم تبشرون

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza read يحسبن with yāʾ; Ibn Qutayba says the intended construction would instead be ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا.
rows.anchor: حمزة. ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says this catalogue of disputed readings is extensive but outside this book's purpose, referring readers to his dedicated work on readings.
rows.anchor: لم يكن القصد في هذا الكتاب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular forms can refer to groups: the hypocrites are العدو, the others رفيقا, one poem calls a group المولى, and another says إنا أخوكم.
rows.anchor: هم المولى وإن جنفوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural can take a singular attribute: جنب, ظهير, and قوم عدل; Zuhayr's رضا and عدل and other poems' أمير and هدي illustrate the same agreement by sense.
rows.anchor: أن تصف الجميع صفة الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single object can be described by plural forms: برمة أعشار, ثوب أهدام وأسمال, نعل أسماط, and a poet's قميصي أخلاق.
rows.anchor: نعل أسماط، أي غير مطبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When two things are joined, an action belonging to one may be attributed to both, as in the paired subjects of the fish-forgetting verse.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir identifies Yushaʿ b. Nun as the one who forgot the fish, supported by his companion's statement in 18:63.
rows.anchor: روي في التفسير: أن الناسي كان يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers addressed jointly to jinn and humans are from humans only.
rows.anchor: والرسل من الإنس دون الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired-seas wording attributes pearls and ornaments to both, though they come only from salt water; Abu Dhuʾayb errs in saying the Euphrates rests above a pearl.
rows.anchor: إنما يخرجان من الماء الملح لا من العذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The converse also occurs: when two things are joined, an action may be assigned to one or attributed to one although it belongs to both.
rows.anchor: أن يجتمع شيئان فيجعل الفعل لأحدهما

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna reports that a Kufa imam recited al-Fil and Quraysh continuously without distinguishing them, prompting some to treat them as one sura.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عيينة أنه قال: كان لنا إمام بالكوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba sides with the majority that al-Fil and Quraysh are two suras as in the codex, despite connected wording through Arabic taḍmīn.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الناس على أنهما سورتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh lived safely in the sanctuary and could trade safely outside it; in a barren valley, they depended on winter caravans to Yemen and summer caravans to Syria.
rows.anchor: أن قريشا كانت بالحرم آمنة من الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the people of the elephant when they sought to demolish the Kaaba and move its stones to Yemen for a rival sanctuary, preserving Quraysh's residence and honor beside the House.
rows.anchor: قصد أصحاب الفيل إلى مكة ليهدموا الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لإيلاف explains that the elephant army was destroyed so God could secure Quraysh's two sustaining journeys; ألفت موضع means I stayed there, and آلفنيه الله means God made me stay.
rows.anchor: فعل ذلك ليؤلف قريشا هاتين الرحلتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated لإيلاف is emphatic repetition, like giving money to preserve someone's face, preservation from everyone.
rows.anchor: أعطيتك المال لصيانة وجهك صيانة عن كل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling these favors, the sura commands Quraysh to worship the Lord of the House who fed them.
rows.anchor: ثم أمرهم بالشكر فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation purpose refers to believers among jinn and humans, as 7:179 says many of them were created for Hell.
rows.anchor: خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address to the messengers is intended for the Prophet alone.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الرسل كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural expression can denote one or more: طائفة may be one person or more, while إخوة in the inheritance rule means two siblings or more.
rows.anchor: طائفة من المؤمنين [النور: 2] : واحد واثنان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says طائفة refers to one man who would not join the group's remarks about the Prophet and kept apart from them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله تعالى: إن نعف عن طائفة

words: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says one man called the Prophet from beyond the rooms, boasting that his praise beautified and his insult disgraced; the Prophet replied that this belonged to God, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وكان «قتادة» يقول في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir says the tablets Moses cast down were two tablets.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: أنهما لوحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural قلوبكما denotes the two hearts belonging to the two women addressed.
rows.anchor: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural referent is Aisha and Safwan b. al-Muʿattal.
rows.anchor: يعني عائشة وصفوان بن المعطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural المرسلون refers to one envoy, as the next verse addresses him with singular ارجع إليهم.
rows.anchor: وهو واحد، يدلك على ذلك قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular may stand for a group: ضيف, رسول, and طفل appear in singular form for plural referents.
rows.anchor: وقوله: نا رسول رب العالمين

words: لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد is singular although distinguishing messengers necessarily involves two or more.
rows.anchor: والتفريق لا يكون إلا بين اثنين فصاعدا

words: فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines singular أحد with plural حاجزين.
rows.anchor: فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary Arabic, كثير الدرهم والدينار means having many dirhams and dinars, using singular nouns collectively.
rows.anchor: فلان كثير الدرهم والدينار، يريدون الدراهم والدنانير

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: The author's father thought the regular qunut supplication was Quran because he saw the Prophet repeat it in prayer, and held to this despite the Companions' disagreement.
rows.anchor: يدعو به في الصلاة دعاء دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba doubts the report that Abdullah omitted Fatiha from his codex and says no Muslim should infer that this learned, Quran-devoted Companion did not know it was Quran.
rows.anchor: فإني أشك فيما روي عن عبد الله من تركه إثباتها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet praised Abdullah's recitation, telling people who wanted the Quran fresh as revealed to follow Ibn Umm ʿAbd's reading.
rows.anchor: النبي) صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول: «من أحب

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar described Abdullah as a container filled with knowledge, supporting Ibn Qutayba's case for his learning.
rows.anchor: وعمر يقول فيه: كنيف ملىء علما

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement لا صلاة إلا بسورة الحمد supports Fatiha's indispensable place in prayer.
rows.anchor: رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يؤم بها، وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatiha is the seven oft-repeated and Mother of the Book, meaning its greatest and earliest part; Mecca is similarly called Mother of Villages because it is oldest.
rows.anchor: أم الكتاب، أي أعظمه، وأقدم ما نزل منه

rows.speaker: أهل النظر
rows.claim: The theorists explain that Abdullah did not write Fatiha because compilation guarded against doubt, forgetting, additions, and omissions, while it was short and repeated every prayer and rakʿa.
rows.anchor: أهل النظر، إلى القرآن إنما كتب وجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba concludes that Abdullah knew Fatiha was Quran but saw no need to write it, since no Muslim could neglect learning it or praying with it.
rows.anchor: ترك كتابتها وهو يعلم أنها من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا is an attention particle, treated as extra in utterance; in ألا إن القوم خارجون it means understand or know that the matter is so.
rows.anchor: تنبيه: وهي زيادة في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet leaves the second alternative unstated after أهم هممته; Ibn Qutayba cites the line as ellipsis.
rows.anchor: أراك فما أدري أهم هممته

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's question أرشد طلابها omits the alternative أم غي, supplied by Ibn Qutayba.
rows.anchor: أبو ذؤيب : عصيت إليها القلب إني لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the description of blackened faces, the omitted words are فيقال لهم before أكفرتم؟
rows.anchor: فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech verb is omitted: the criminals say ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا.
rows.anchor: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسوا رؤسهم عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits يقولان before Abraham and Ishmael's prayer, understood as they both say ربنا تقبل منا.
rows.anchor: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line means that when night came, the donkeys raised their ears; أقبل is omitted before الليل.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة يصف حميرا :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's أن لا إلى أم سالم omits سبيل, meaning there is no way to reach Umm Salim.
rows.anchor: وقد بدا لذي نهية أن لا إلى أم سالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه, the command to show kindness to parents omits وصى, understood from context.
rows.anchor: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: النمر بن تولب
rows.claim: In al-Namir b. Tawlab's line, أينما omits ذهب: wherever the person goes, he will encounter the feared thing.
rows.anchor: النمر بن تولب : فإن المنبه من يخشها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عاصف means a day of fierce wind; the verse omits الريح because it was already mentioned.
rows.anchor: كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause means nor can those in heaven escape; من في السماء is understood after ولا في السماء.
rows.anchor: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' hand is counted among the nine signs: في تسع آيات means in or together with these signs.
rows.anchor: وأدخل يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء في تسع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After إلى فرعون, مرسلا or مبعوثا is omitted because the mission is understood.
rows.anchor: إلى فرعون ولم يقل مرسلا ولا مبعوثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commissioning verb is omitted in وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا; the meaning is أرسلنا إلى ثمود.
rows.anchor: ومثله: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's رأتني بحبليها omits مقبلا: she saw me approaching with the two ropes.
rows.anchor: رأتني بحبليها فصدت مخافة

words: فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوؤا وجوهكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba begins another ellipsis example from this verse, but this extracted segment ends before supplying the omitted wording.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوؤا وجوهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor's source is a stairway: one ascends or descends rung by rung, and this concrete sense is borrowed for درجات.
rows.anchor: من الدرجة، وذلك أن الراقي فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويقبضون أيديهم means withholding gifts; the image comes from a giver extending and opening a hand, so a miser is said to close his hand.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا: أن المعطي بيده يمدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews' claim that God's hand is bound means that He withholds, extending the hand metaphor for stinginess to divine speech.
rows.anchor: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being surrounded means approaching destruction, as an encircled enemy or town nears ruin; the same image describes the garden's lost fruit.
rows.anchor: أي دنوا من الهلاك. وأصل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs poetically say sun, moon, wind, sky, and earth wept for a great benefactor to magnify a loss; listeners understand the convention, so it is not a lie, and كاد means nearly did but did not.
rows.anchor: تقول العرب إذا أرادت تعظيم مهلك رجل عظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: ابن مفرغ الحميري
rows.claim: Ibn Mufarrigh al-Himyari's image of the wind weeping and lightning flashing illustrates poetic personification of grief.
rows.anchor: ابن مفرغ الحميري يرثي رجلا : الريح تبكي شجوه

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says the rising sun weeps while night stars and moon mourn; كاسفة cannot mean eclipsing them in daylight, since its light would eclipse them.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : الشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's battle scene, where stars appear while the sun is up and neither light nor darkness is itself, illustrates the same hyperbolic obscurity.
rows.anchor: كقوله النابغة وذكر يوم حرب

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Tarafa says the beloved can make a man see stars at noon, meaning she torments him until his day seems dark.
rows.anchor: قول طرفة في وصف امرأة : إن تنوله فقد تمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Curses such as قتل الخراصون, قتل الإنسان, and قاتلهم الله express blame, not a wish that the stated harm literally occur.
rows.anchor: كقول الله عز وجل: قتل الخراصون

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet called a woman عقرى حلقى, an idiomatic imprecation wishing barrenness and throat pain.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، للمرأة: «عقرى حلقى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same curse formulas can express amazement and praise at excellent speech, poetry, argument, or marksmanship rather than a literal wish of harm.
rows.anchor: قاتله الله ما أحسن ما قال

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's archer poem says the man is not counted among his people, an exaggerated way of saying may God kill him for his astonishing shot.
rows.anchor: امرئ القيس في وصف رام أصاب : فهو لا تنمي رميته

rows.speaker: كعب بن سعد الغنوي
rows.claim: Kaʿb b. Saʿd al-Ghanawi's هوت أمه is another conventional imprecation; the poet marvels at the man's extraordinary journeys.
rows.anchor: كعب بن سعد الغنوي : هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciprocal terms such as mock, scheme, evil, and aggression name God's requital: the first aggression is injustice, while the answering act is just punishment.
rows.anchor: إنما نحن مستهزؤن (14) الله يستهزئ بهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a prayer against someone who satirized him, the Prophet asked for a curse matching the number or place of the satire, meaning requital for it.
rows.anchor: قول النبي) صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اللهم إن فلانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgetting the hypocrites means leaving or requiting them, using their own forgetfulness of God as reciprocal language.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله: نسوا الله فنسيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questions may function as confirmation rather than requests for unknown information, as in questions to Jesus, Moses, and communities addressed by messengers.
rows.anchor: على مذهب الاستفهام وهو تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الصلاة means supplication: pray for them, since the Prophet's prayer calms them and reassures their hearts.
rows.anchor: ادع لهم، إن ذلك مما يسكنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صلوات الرسول means the Messenger's supplications.
rows.anchor: ويتخذ ما ينفق قربات عند الله وصلوات الرسول

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: In al-Aʿsha's wine poem, وصلى على دنها means he prayed that the wine cask avoid spoilage and change.
rows.anchor: الأعشى يذكر الخمر والخمار : وقابلها الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's الصلاة is mercy and forgiveness, as shown by verses pairing divine prayers with mercy and by God's and the angels' prayers for the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: والصلاة من الله: الرحمة والمغفرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's prayer for the family of Abu Awfa asks God to show them mercy and forgive them.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اللهم صل على آل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Shuʿayb use الصلاة to mean religion when they mockingly ask whether it commands him to abandon ancestral worship.
rows.anchor: أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصلاة is also said to mean recitation in the question about Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: والصلاة: الدين. قال تعالى حكاية عن قوم شعيب: أصلاتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متكأ names food metaphorically: a host prepares a cushion so a guest can stay comfortably, then the food is named for the place of reclining; Jamil's poem uses the reclining image.
rows.anchor: وقال جميل : فظللنا بنعمة واتكأنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock means subduing and humiliating it through sovereign power; ناصيتي بيدك likewise means You own and overpower me.
rows.anchor: أي يقهرها ويذلها بالملك والسلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remaining قائم عليه means persistently pursuing payment, since a claimant stands and acts while one who abandons the claim sits back.
rows.anchor: أن المطالب بالشيء يقوم فيه ويتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's يقوم على الوغم describes pursuing a blood claim without abandoning it, illustrating the metaphor of standing for persistence.
rows.anchor: يقوم على الوغم في قومه ... فيعفو إذا شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمة قائمة means an active community that does not abandon its work.
rows.anchor: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة

words: قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is قائم over every soul in the sense that He takes it to account for what it has earned.
rows.anchor: أي آخذ لها بما كسبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' claim that Muhammad is an ear means he accepts every report he hears; the ear is metaphorically named for the credulous listener.
rows.anchor: أي يقبل كل ما بلغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With فأذنوا the command means know of a war from God; the alternate reading فآذنوا means announce or notify one another.
rows.anchor: أي اعلموا، ومن قرأها (فآذنوا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root means informing: آذنتك فأذنت means I told you and you heard; al-Aʿsha's line and the call to prayer use أذان for announcement.
rows.anchor: أعلمتك فعلمت، إنما هو أوقعته في أذنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that Muhammad is an ear for good: he trusts God and believers, not the hypocrites who expect their excuses to be accepted.
rows.anchor: أي كان الأمر كما تذكرون، ولكنه إنما يؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this phrase, Ibn Qutayba regards the bāʾ and lām as extra particles.
rows.anchor: لا أنتم، (والباء) و (اللام) زائدتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضرب can mean striking with the hand, as in commands about necks and wives.
rows.anchor: وقوله: واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضرب can mean traveling or journeying.
rows.anchor: والضرب: المسير، قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضرب can mean explaining or describing: making a parable, or describing God with attributes of others, which the verse forbids.
rows.anchor: والضرب: التبيين والوصف، قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poem jussives وأستدرج by carrying over the syntactic position of أصالحكم, understood without the preceding لعلي.
rows.anchor: فجزم وأستدرج، وحمله على موضع أصالحكم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr read فأصدق وأكون in the subjunctive and argued that the copyist dropped wāw, as long vowels are omitted in spellings such as كلمون.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو بن العلاء يقرأ: فأصدق وأكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says disputed forms either follow accepted grammar or reflect scribal spelling; in the first case Quran has no grammatical error, and in the second the scribe's fault is not the Messenger's.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت على مذاهب النحويين فليس هاهنا لحن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha is cited for the view that some disputed forms are mistakes made by the copyist.
rows.anchor: كما ذكرت عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex omits the dual alif in إن هذان and writes dual forms such as رجلن and فآخران without it, showing irregular script is not a Quranic defect.
rows.anchor: كتب في الإمام: إن هذان لساحران بحذف ألف التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex writes الصلاة, الزكوة, and الحيوة with wāw; although القطاة, القناة, and الفلاة use alif, Ibn Qutayba sees no difference.
rows.anchor: كتاب المصحف: الصلاة والزكوة والحيوة، بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex writes الربو with wāw and فمال with a single detached lām, further orthographic examples.
rows.anchor: الذين كفروا [المعارج: 36] فمال بلام منفردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex writes نبإ المرسلين and من وراء حجاب with yāʾ although neither contains a yāʾ sound; the letter represents kasra.
rows.anchor: ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم لهم شركاء and فقال الضعفاء are written with wāw and no preceding alif, more evidence of spelling convention.
rows.anchor: وفقال الضعفاء [إبراهيم: 21] بواو، ولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex writes ما نشؤا with wāw after alif in Shuʿayb's verse, while the same form elsewhere lacks wāw, without a difference in meaning.
rows.anchor: بواو بعد الألف، وفي موضع آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex adds an alif in لأذبحنه and another after the lam-alif in ولأوضعوا.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ولأوضعوا خلالكم [التوبة: 47]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differences of tongues and colors mean differences in languages, outward appearances, and forms.
rows.anchor: اختلاف، اللغات، والمناظر، والهيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are gathered and moving, but their immensity makes them seem still to an observer; they travel like clouds.
rows.anchor: أنها تجمع وتسير، فهي لكثرتها كأنها جامدة

rows.speaker: الجعدي
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿdi compares an immense moving army to a mountain: it looks stopped to the eye while mounts move, illustrating the mountains' apparent stillness.
rows.anchor: الجعدي في وصف جيش فقال : بأرعن مثل الطود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation preserves life because punishing a killer deters would-be killers, so the threat of killing protects people.
rows.anchor: سافك الدم إذا أقيد منه ارتدع من كان يهم بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet applies the life-in-retribution idea to reproach: mutual admonition repairs relations and prevents killing; proverbs say some killing revives all and killing reduces killing.
rows.anchor: وفي العتاب حياة بين أقوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired descriptions of heavenly wine deny its defects; ولا ينزفون covers loss of reason, wealth, and drink.
rows.anchor: عدم العقل، وذهاب المال، ونفاد الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast ranks hearing above sight: deafness is paired with lack of reason, while blindness is paired only with inability to see.
rows.anchor: فضل السمع على البصر، حين جعل مع الصمم فقدان العقل

words: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditions set for hypocrites' repentance show they are worse than other disbelievers, more deserving of wrath and farther from return to God.
rows.anchor: المنافقين شر من كفر به، وأولاهم بمقته، وأبعدهم
